newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador to sell 35 pct of phone co shares April 28.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador to sell 35 pct of phone co shares April 28.

text.p: Ecuador's government will sell 35 percent of its 100 percent holding in telephone company Empresa Estatal de Telecomunicaciones on April 28, 1997, local press reported Tuesday.
"The tender will take place on April 28. The highest bidder gets the company," Leonardo Escobar, director of the National Council of Modernization, told newspaper El Comercio.
According to El Comercio, the auction could draw as much $3.0 billion in bids. No base price has been set for the sale.
The privatization process of the state telephone company was begun under the administration of former president Sixto Duran Ballen, and current President Abdala Bucaram has put the sale into effect.
The government has said bidders in the contest include MCI-International Communications Corp of the U.S., Telefonica de Espana SA, STET of Italy, GTE of the U.S. and Korea Telecom.
Escobar added that in January government officials will travel to London and New York to meet potential bidders.
